anatomy.flutter: Carousel (Focus + Semantics region) containing an OverflowBox/Stack of _Track (the -ml-4 gutter track + GestureDetector, equivalent to CarouselContent/CarouselItem) and two _Arrow widgets (equivalent to CarouselPrevious/CarouselNext), driven by a CarouselController that reimplements Embla's engine.
anatomy.web: Carousel (role=region, aria-roledescription=carousel) > CarouselContent (overflow-hidden viewport + -ml-4 flex track) > CarouselItem (pl-4, basis-full) repeated, plus CarouselPrevious/CarouselNext as absolutely positioned Buttons, all wired through useEmblaCarousel via CarouselContext.

api.flutter: Carousel({basis, items, padding, previousLabel, nextLabel}) -- a single fixed-axis (horizontal only) widget with no orientation prop, no opts/plugins passthrough, and no setApi/imperative controller exposed to the caller (CarouselController exists but is private to the widget's State).
api.web: Carousel({orientation: "horizontal"|"vertical", opts, plugins, setApi, ...}) -- full Embla options/plugins passthrough and an imperative CarouselApi handed back via setApi for external control.
api.note: Reclassified on review from `gap`: the shortfall recorded below is on the FLUTTER side — the web has the capability, or Flutter's own doc comment records it as not ported, or Flutter reproduces an earlier state of the web source that has since moved on. This ledger measures the web's convergence onto Flutter's vocabulary, so it is a pass here. The worker's original finding is kept verbatim after this line, because the finding is still true and still worth a Flutter reader's attention. ORIGINAL: The Flutter port is horizontal-only (CarouselContent's -mt-4/flex-col vertical branch and CarouselItem's pt-4 vertical branch have no Dart equivalent at all), and there is no way for a Flutter caller to pass Embla-equivalent options or plugins, nor to get an external handle on the controller the way `setApi` provides on the web. This is a real, usable-API gap rather than an unexercised corner: any product screen needing a vertical carousel or external prev/next control from outside the widget tree has nothing to reach for.

states.flutter: CarouselController tracks canScrollPrev/canScrollNext (index bounds against the trimmed snap ladder), selectedIndex, and a dragging flag; _Arrow disables itself via Button's own disabled state when its direction cannot scroll -- reproduced from a measured rAF trace of Embla's integrator, rubber-band bounds, and trimSnaps ladder.
states.web: useEmblaCarousel's canScrollPrev()/canScrollNext() drive CarouselPrevious/CarouselNext's disabled prop directly; Embla itself owns drag/rubber-band/snap state.

disabled.flutter: _Arrow passes onPressed: enabled ? handler : null to Button, so a boundary arrow renders through Button's own disabled skin/cursor and explains itself via that shared control (documented as the reason no separate hit-area expander is needed at the clipped edge).
disabled.web: CarouselPrevious/CarouselNext pass disabled={!canScrollPrev} / disabled={!canScrollNext} straight to the shared Button component, which owns the disabled visual/semantic treatment.

interaction.flutter: _Track's GestureDetector only wires onHorizontalDragStart/Update/End/Cancel (pointer drag) plus _onKey for ArrowLeft/ArrowRight on the region's Focus node; there is no separate touch-vs-mouse distinction and no documented swipe/fling velocity projection (dragEnd() snaps to nearest snap point by distance only, not velocity, which the doc comment states plainly: '−100 returned to 0 ... nothing here needs a velocity projection').
interaction.web: Embla's pointer/touch handling includes its own velocity-based release behaviour in addition to nearest-snap logic (Embla's ScrollBody physics beyond what dragEnd's nearest-snap alone reproduces), and the wrapper adds onKeyDownCapture for ArrowLeft/ArrowRight identically to the Flutter port.
interaction.note: Reclassified on review from `gap`: the shortfall recorded below is on the FLUTTER side — the web has the capability, or Flutter's own doc comment records it as not ported, or Flutter reproduces an earlier state of the web source that has since moved on. This ledger measures the web's convergence onto Flutter's vocabulary, so it is a pass here. The worker's original finding is kept verbatim after this line, because the finding is still true and still worth a Flutter reader's attention. ORIGINAL: The Flutter doc comment itself states that the measured release behaviour only needed nearest-snap distance, not velocity, for the two data points it drove (-100 and -200 px holds). This is a narrower behavioural claim than Embla's full physics engine generally provides (Embla does incorporate release velocity into its target selection in the general case), so the port's dragEnd is a simplification that was validated for the two cases probed but is not proven equivalent across the full velocity space. Recorded as gap rather than platform-difference because this is an unverified simplification of shared (not platform-specific) physics, not a deliberate different-but-correct mechanism.

semantics.flutter: Carousel wraps its Focus in Semantics(container: true, label: 'carousel'); _Arrow's Button carries its own label (previousLabel/nextLabel, default 'Previous slide'/'Next slide').
semantics.web: Carousel div carries role="region" aria-roledescription="carousel"; CarouselItem carries role="group" aria-roledescription="slide"; CarouselPrevious/Next carry sr-only 'Previous slide'/'Next slide' spans.
